name: The Bunya Pine of the Arcos do Jardim

location.address: Jardim Botanico da Universidade de Coimbra, entered beside the Arcos do Jardim (Aqueduto de Sao Sebastiao), Calcada Martim de Freitas, Coimbra
location.neighbourhood: Almedina, within the University Botanical Garden

verified_sources: ICNF Arvoredo de Interesse Publico register (si.icnf.pt/wfs/arv_class, CC BY 4.0), processo KNJ1/571, classified Aviso n.o 25 de 29/12/2010
access: Paid entry, University of Coimbra Botanical Garden ticket; reached through the Arcos do Jardim gate under the aqueduct arches.
transport: 5-10 minute walk from Praca da Republica / central Coimbra.
verify_notes: ICNF register (processo KNJ1/571): girth 6.3m, height 19m, crown 16.6m, age_register 150 as measured in 2010, so roughly 165-166 by 2026 (register age plus years since). Publico's 2018 feature on the Botanical Garden's 'treasures' independently describes the garden's upper terrace as holding centenarian, large trees, 'some 150 years old', and specifically names the garden's seven araucaria species growing there, which is consistent with but not a fresh remeasurement of the register figure. Classified as tree of public interest by Aviso n.o 25 de 29/12/2010. The garden's own page (uc.pt/jardimbotanico) returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl and was not used as a source. Remarkable fact for the writer: the garden holds seven araucaria species and thirty eucalyptus species, called out in English-language Wikipedia (citing Thomas Pakenham's 'Remarkable Trees of the World') as home to a notable Ficus macrophylla too, so this bunya sits among a genuinely exceptional exotic-tree collection dating to the 19th century.

name: The Karri Knight

location.address: Mata Nacional de Vale de Canas, Torres do Mondego, Coimbra

verified_sources: ICNF Arvoredo de Interesse Publico register, processo KNJ1/415, classified D.R. n.o 188, II Serie de 16/08/2002
access: Free; inside the Mata Nacional de Vale de Canas, a small enclosed national forest with a marked path from a small parking area.
transport: About 3.6 km from central Coimbra (car or taxi), then roughly a 15-minute walk from the parking area.
verify_notes: ICNF register (KNJ1/415): girth 5.78m, height 72.9m, crown 30.5m, age_register 140 (measured 2015). monumentaltrees.com's archived Vale de Canas page independently lists 'Karri Knight' at the same location: girth 6.03m @1.30m, height ~75.2m, so girth figures disagree modestly (5.78m vs 6.03m) while height corroborates closely. luamarte.wordpress.com (an October 2021 visit account) separately reports 'approximately 140 years and 75 metres', cites a 2017 laser measurement by the Giant Trees Foundation of 73m, and says it 'reportedly' (terra sido, i.e. not stated as certain) was planted in 1873 by the Mondego Hydraulic Services. Widely and repeatedly described in independent sources (search results referencing Atlas Obscura and others) as the tallest tree in Europe / the Iberian Peninsula; Atlas Obscura's own page 403'd this pass and was not used as a source. Do not sharpen the 1873 planting date into a firm age given the source's own hedging.

name: The Bunya Knight

location.address: Mata Nacional de Vale de Canas, Torres do Mondego, Coimbra, close to the Karri Knight

verified_sources: ICNF Arvoredo de Interesse Publico register, processo KNJ1/416, classified D.R. n.o 188, II Serie de 16/08/2002
access: Free; same Mata Nacional de Vale de Canas forest as the Karri Knight, a few dozen metres away on the same path.
transport: Same as the Karri Knight: about 3.6 km from central Coimbra, then a roughly 15-minute walk from the parking area.
verify_notes: ICNF register (KNJ1/416): girth 3.7m, height 54m, crown 17.7m, age_register 140 (measured 2015), standing near the Karri Knight in the same forest. monumentaltrees.com's archived Vale de Canas page corroborates: 'Bunya Knight' girth 3.88m, height ~54m, explicitly described as standing right next to the Karri Knight, and called the largest of its species in Portugal. luamarte.wordpress.com (2021) gives a different height, 49m, and describes the species as sacred to Australian Aboriginal peoples, a good anecdote for the writer; treat its 49m figure as a minor disagreement against the register/monumentaltrees consensus of 54m.

name: The Camphor Tree of ESAC

location.address: ESAC - Escola Superior Agraria de Coimbra campus, Bencanta, Sao Martinho do Bispo, Coimbra (behind the Bencanta railway station)

verified_sources: ICNF Arvoredo de Interesse Publico register, processo KNJ1/170, classified D.G. n.o 173, II Serie de 25/07/1969
access: On the campus of a public higher-education institution (ESAC, part of the Instituto Politecnico de Coimbra); visible from campus paths, but general walk-in access by the public is NOT independently confirmed this pass. ESAC's own site routes visit requests through its external relations office (gac@esac.pt). Ship with this caveat stated plainly, or confirm access before publishing.
transport: Near the Bencanta railway station (Linha do Norte, Coimbra suburban services), about 3.7 km from central Coimbra.
verify_notes: ICNF register (KNJ1/170): girth 8.5m, height 28m, crown 34.5m, age_register 163 (measured 2015). Independently, ESAC's own news page (esac.pt, 4 Dec 2025) reports the tree as one of ten finalists for Portugal's 'Arvore do Ano 2026' public vote, states it was planted in 1860 and is 'currently 165 years old' (i.e. as stated in Dec 2025; call it roughly 165-166 by 2026), over 28m tall (an exact match to the register's height figure) with a trunk perimeter 'exceeding 9 metres' (vs the register's 8.5m, plausible extra growth over the ~10 years between measurements). The two sources give slightly different age bases (register-derived ~174 by 2026 vs ESAC's documented-planting-date ~165-166); this record uses the documented planting date as the more reliable basis per the estimating hierarchy and flags the register's higher figure. Notable and current: ESAC's Dec 2025 piece says the tree is potentially threatened by the planned route of a future high-speed rail line, worth a line in the story since its future is not guaranteed. ACCESS remains the open question, see the access field; do not upgrade the caveat away without new evidence.
